title: No injuries reported so far; loco pilot failed to control train’s speed while giving precedence to another train, authorities said
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Several coaches of Kolkata-Sairang Express train derailed at Digaru railway station in Assam early Wednesday (November 11, 2026) after the loco pilot failed to control the train’s speed while giving precedence to another train.

Assam train derailment LIVE updates

All passengers are safe and no injuries were reported, Northeast Frontier Railway said.

#WATCH | Assam: A locomotive and five coaches of the Kolkata-Sairang Express (Train No. 13125) derailed at Digaru Railway Station in Kamrup (Metro) district at around 6:54 am today. According to Northeast Frontier Railway, all passengers are safe, and no injuries have been reported. Passengers are being transported to their destinations by an alternative train. Relief and rescue operations have been launched. (Visuals from the spot)

— ANI (@ANI) November 11, 2026

The train, enroute to Kolkata from Sairang near Mizoram’s Aizawl, derailed near Digaru railway station in Kamrup (Metropolitan) district around 6.54 a.m., resulting in the derailment of six coaches, including the locomotive.

Relief and rescue operations are under way, the Indian Railways zone said, adding that passengers are being taken to their destinations by an alternate train.

The exact cause of derailment is yet to be ascertained.

With PTI inputs

title: Army jawan posted with President’s Bodyguard shot in U.P.; condition stable
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
A man posted as Army jawan in the Rashtrapati Bhavan security was allegedly shot by two neighbours following an old rivalry in Uttar Pradesh’s Baghpat district on Deepavali night.

Saurabh Tomar (26), serving in the elite President’s Bodyguard (PBG) regiment, underwent surgery at a private hospital in Meerut and is said to be stable. The bullet struck Mr. Tomar just behind the ear, the police said. His brother also suffered serious head injuries after being attacked with a stick.

The police have registered a case at Ramala police station against two accused and formed three police teams to arrest them, who remained at large.

A resident of the village, Mr. Tomar was recruited in 2021 and is currently posted at the Rashtrapati Bhavan. He was visiting the village on leave to celebrate Deepavali. On Sunday night (November 8, 2026), he was bursting firecrackers outside his home along with his brothers Vineet and Mintu when an argument allegedly broke out with two villagers, Dheeraj and his brother Monu alias Praveen.

“On 08.11.2026 at 9:45 p.m., Ramala police station received information that in village Gopalpur Khadana, Monu alias Praveen and Dheeraj, residents of the same village, fired a shot which ricocheted off the wall and hit the plaintiff’s son Saurabh (serving in Rashtrapati Bhavan security), injuring him. Vineet was also hit on the head with a stick and injured,” a statement by the Baghpat police read.

The complaint was filed by the Mr. Tomar’s father Janak Raj. “On receiving the information, Ramala police station immediately registered an FIR. Saurabh is undergoing treatment in a Meerut hospital. Both are in normal condition. Based on the complaint of the plaintiff/father Janak Raj, a case has been registered at Ramala police station. Three police teams have been formed to arrest the accused, and efforts are being made by them to arrest them,” the statement added.

The President's Bodyguard is the oldest and senior-most cavalry regiment in the Indian Army, stationed at the Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi.

With PTI inputs

title: Sonia Gandhi’s book attempts to give her family clean chit over 1984 anti-Sikh massacre: BJP
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) alleged that former Congress president Sonia Gandhi, through her book, attempted to shield former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and the Congress leadership from responsibility for the 1984 anti-Sikh massacre.

At a press briefing, senior BJP leader Harvinder Singh Phoolka said: “In the book that Sonia Gandhi has published, she has tried to give her family a clean chit over the massacre of Sikhs.” He alleged that the book’s account, which was in “complete contradiction of the official record”, wrongly attributed the delay in deploying the Army to General A.S. Vaidya.

“First, as per the Misra Commission’s report, 6,100 soldiers were available in Delhi on the night of October 31 and the morning of November 1, but they were not deployed in time. The Commission also wrote that if 5,000 of these soldiers had been made to march through Delhi’s streets on the morning of November 1, at least 2,000 Sikhs could have been saved. Both the Misra Commission and the Nanavati Commission made the same point in their reports,” he said.

“The Misra Commission says that even if Rajiv Gandhi had alerted General Vaidya, the Army Chief’s job is only to keep the Army ready, while administrative officials are responsible for calling in the Army and deploying it in the field. The administrative machinery neither called in the Army in time nor deployed it,” said Mr. Phoolka.

“Rajiv Gandhi was the country’s Prime Minister at the time. If he was not directly responsible himself, what action did he take against those who failed to mobilise the Army present in Delhi on the morning of November 1? Instead, at his first public rally, Rajiv Gandhi said: ‘When a big tree falls, the earth shakes a little.’ In this way, he tried to justify the entire massacre,” he said.

Union Minister Giriraj Singh accused Ms. Gandhi of being selective in expressing grief over incidents such as Babri and Batla House, but not over the Godhra and Pahalgam incidents. He said her book should have addressed what he described as former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru’s mistakes, including Tibet and Articles 370 and 35A.

BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari alleged that the book reflected the Congress’s “vote-bank politics”, which would lead to another electoral defeat for the principal Opposition party in 2029.

title: RSS activist seeks FIR against Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge over arms seizure post
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
A city-based RSS activist has lodged a police complaint against Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge at the Banashankari police station, seeking the registration of an FIR over an alleged social media post linking the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) to a major seizure of arms and ammunition.

The complaint was submitted on November 10, 2026 by Tejas A. Gowda, a Bengaluru resident and RSS activist. He accused Mr. Kharge of allegedly circulating “misleading” information through his official X handle and attempting to disturb social harmony by associating the RSS with the seizure of around 44,250 live cartridges in Bihar and Haryana.

In his complaint, Mr. Gowda alleged that the Minister’s statements and insinuations created an impression that the RSS was connected to criminal activities, potentially triggering hostility and disturbing communal harmony.

He has sought action against theMminister under Sections 192, 196 and 353 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.

“Holding a constitutional office does not confer immunity from criminal law,” Mr. Gowda stated, urging the police to act independently and without political interference.

The complainant has also requested the police to preserve electronic records of the social media posts, obtain details of the ammunition seizure cases from police authorities in Bihar and Haryana, and investigate whether misleading information was knowingly disseminated.

The massive seizure of 44,250 live cartridges in Bihar and Haryana has exposed a serious interstate ammunition-smuggling network. This is not an ordinary criminal case. This is a grave national security concern. Even more disturbing are reports and photographs allegedly showing individuals implicated in the racket wearing RSS uniforms. The RSS and BJP owe the nation some answers. 1. WHAT IS THE RSS CONNECTION? Photographs reportedly show accused individuals in RSS uniforms. Were these individuals RSS Swayamsevaks? What positions did they hold in the organisation? If they were Swayamsevaks, what was their involvement in the ammunition racket? What was their intent? Who were they working for? 2. WHERE WERE 44,250 LIVE CARTRIDGES HEADED? This is enough ammunition to facilitate violence on a massive scale. Who were the intended recipients? Were these cartridges destined for organised criminal networks, extremist groups or other unlawful activities? 3. HOW DID GOVERNMENT-MANUFACTURED AMMUNITION ENTER THE ILLEGAL MARKET? Reports indicate that the seized cartridges bore markings associated with the Khadki ammunition factory in Pune. Who facilitated the diversion of this ammunition? Which licensed arms dealers and intermediaries were involved? How long has this network been operating, and how extensive is it? 4. WHY ARE THE BJP AND RSS SILENT? The BJP never misses an opportunity to lecture the country on nationalism, patriotism and national security. Yet, when individuals allegedly associated with RSS come under scrutiny in a massive ammunition-smuggling investigation, where is the outrage? Where is the accountability? 5. THIS IS PRECISELY WHY THE RSS MUST BE REGISTERED! An organisation cannot claim millions of Swayamsevaks when it suits its interests and conveniently disown individuals when serious criminal allegations emerge. Registration and proper membership records would strengthen accountability and make organisational associations easier to verify. The RSS demands accountability from everyone else. Why should it be exempt from the same scrutiny? @DrMohanBhagwat ji, I would be more than happy to personally facilitate the RSS's registration and even pay the registration fees myself.

— Priyank Kharge / ಪ್ರಿಯಾಂಕ್ ಖರ್ಗೆ (@PriyankKharge) November 10, 2026

Copies of posts from Mr. Kharge’s X account and another social media handle titled ‘Fact Myths’ were enclosed with the complaint.

Police acknowledged receiving the complaint, but no FIR had been registered at the time of reporting. Mr Kharge is yet to issue a statement on the matter.
